label: Asset Afterlife factual documentary
viewer_promise: Follow a valuable object after its final public moment and reveal who controls it, what remains valuable, what decisions determine its fate, and where it ultimately goes.

planner_roles.semantic: a production semantic planner for a sourced longform factual documentary
planner_roles.editorial: an editorial beat director for timed factual documentary narration about the hidden afterlife of valuable objects
planner_roles.reference: a documentary visual-reference director preserving real-world asset, location, process, and custody continuity
planner_roles.visual_prompt: a precise factual-documentary reconstruction and technical-visualization prompt planner

voice.pause_contract: Natural sentence and paragraph punctuation provides documentary pacing; explicit dramatic pause directives are optional.

reference_kind_instructions.style: 16:9 landscape cinematic factual-documentary visualization sample with physically plausible materials, restrained editorial lighting, realistic scale, clean composition, and no baked captions or logos
reference_kind_instructions.character_state: 16:9 landscape documentary reenactment identity plate with exactly one clearly adult worker in practical role-appropriate clothing, neutral pose, plain studio background, and no visible brand marks
reference_kind_instructions.location: 16:9 landscape unoccupied factual-documentary environment plate with physically plausible architecture, workflow geometry, scale, lighting, materials, pathways, and clean space for later subjects
reference_kind_instructions.prop: 16:9 landscape asset continuity plate with exactly one inert real-world object on a neutral surface, physically plausible geometry, materials, wear, scale cues, and no invented logo or readable serial text
reference_kind_instructions.ui: 16:9 landscape technical-documentary diagram or interface motif with simple geometry, restrained color coding, sparse icon language, and no dense generated text
reference_kind_instructions.action: 16:9 landscape factual process-demonstration plate showing one physically plausible operation, movement path, machine relationship, or custody transfer without sensational spectacle

planner_directives: Treat the object as the episode protagonist and preserve its visible make, color, wear, tags, damage, and state across cuts.
Prefer one hero asset, one process relationship, or one evidence object per frame; never solve complexity with a collage.
Show custody, transport, inspection, sorting, valuation, repair, resale, donation, recycling, or destruction through physically plausible cause and effect.
Never invent a company logo, serial number, legal document, price, machine, workflow, or destination that the narration and evidence ledger do not support.
Generated scenes are illustrative reconstructions, not archival footage. Exact labels, figures, routes, and quotations belong in deterministic render overlays.
Use diagrams, maps, object inserts, scale comparisons, and before-after states to vary the first three minutes instead of repeating warehouse tableaux.

hard_rules: Every factual number, legal rule, ownership claim, standard practice, and named destination must map to at least one evidence-ledger claim.
Distinguish standard practice from a named company's process and from an illustrative composite journey.
Do not present generated imagery as a photograph or recording of the documented event.
Do not infer a universal process from one jurisdiction, airline, buyer, or case.

packaging.title_pattern: A complete plain-language question naming the asset and its terminal condition.
packaging.thumbnail_rule: One hero asset, one before-after contrast, one arrow, and no collage.
